column3: Decoder field-extraction macros (get_d5/get_vd5/get_io5/get_h4_k8...) for the AVR instruction word plus the SREG bit-index enum S_C..S_I.

AVR ADC: converts the selected analog pin voltage to a digital value over a scheduled conversion time; wires ADTS auto-trigger to comparator/timer/capture interrupts and implements the ADMUX Vref-selection variants.
Declares AvrAdc plus a type ladder (AvrAdc00/02/03/04/10/11/20) each overriding setup/updtVref/specialConv for a different AVR ADC generation.
AVR analog comparator: compares AIN0/AIN1 (or the 1.1 V bandgap) and raises the comparator interrupt on toggle/rising/falling edge; reading ACSR triggers a re-compare and clears ACO.
Declares AvrComp with the ACSR/AIN0D/AIN1D bit sets and the ACO/ACI/ACIE/ACIC/ACIS register-bit handles.
AVR CPU core: a big switch decoder over the 16-bit instruction word implementing arithmetic/logic/branch/AVR-specific opcodes, with per-opcode cycle accounting and SREG flag helpers.
Declares AvrCore (extends Mcu8bits) with the status-flag helper set, optional RAMPZ/EIND extended-address registers and self-programming SPM bits.
AVR EEPROM: models the EEMPE/EEPE 4-cycle write-enable window and the 1.8/3.4/8.5 ms erase-write cycle via a scheduled Simulator event.
Declares AvrEeprom over McuEeprom, holding the EECR pointer and the EEPM/EEMPE/EEPE/EERE register-bit handles.
AVR input-capture unit: decodes ICES/ICNC to select rising vs falling edge capture; the capture timestamp is taken from the parent timer count.
Declares AvrIcUnit over McuIcUnit with the per-instance ICES/ICNC bit set (suffix taken from the timer name).
AVR interrupt class: currently a thin subclass of the generic Interrupt whose per-family execute/exitInt overrides are commented out.
Declares AVRInterrupt with a static getInterrupt factory; the SREG-I handling it once had is commented out.
AVR internal RC oscillator: derives the CPU frequency from the UI-set frequency divided by the CLKPR prescaler index, calling freqChanged when the index changes.
Declares AvrIntOsc over McuIntOsc with the CLKPS prescaler bit set.
AVR output-compare-modifier: ANDs or ORs the two OC-unit states onto the shared OCM pin depending on the TIMSK mode bit.
Declares AvrOcm over McuOcm with a configureA entry point and an abstract OutputOcm.
AVR output-compare unit: drives the OC pin (or hands control to the OCM), and applies the OCRnx bit-width mask to the compare value.
Declares AvrOcUnit over McuOcUnit with the OCR register width mask and the pin-state override.
AVR pin: on a port-register write it also sets a 100k pull-up (AVR ports have pull-ups), and decodes the external-interrupt trigger mode (ISC bits).
Declares AvrPin over McuPin overriding setPortState and ConfExtInt.
AVR port: a write to the PORT register toggles only the changed bits (outChanged computes the XOR) and the PIN register read is overridden with the live pin state.
Declares AvrPort over McuPort adding pinRegChanged and the AvrPin factory.
AVR sleep modes: reads SM/SE bits, tracks the sleep mode, and detaches the configured wake-up interrupts when sleep is disabled.
Declares AvrSleep over McuSleep with the sleepMode_t enum (idle/ADC/PowerDo/PowerSa/Stand/ExtSt) and the SM/SE bit handles.
AVR SPI: translates SPCR (MSTR/CPOL/CPHA/DODR/SPR) into the shared SpiModule edge/prescaler state, and raises SPIF on transaction end.
Declares AvrSpi over McuSpi with the SPCR/SPSR/SPDR register-bit handles and the 2x speed flag.
AVR timers: the 8/16-bit variants (800/801/810/820/821/822/160) map WGM mode bits onto compare/PWM behaviour and compute the prescaled tick period.
Declares AvrTimer and its variants; the WGM (waveform generation) mode enum and the OCA/OCB/OCC output-compare handles live here.
AVR TWI: turns TWCR/TWBR/TWAR/TWSR/TWDR writes into master start/stop/read/write, sets the TWWC write-collision bit, and publishes the AVR TWI status codes into TWSR.
Declares AvrTwi over McuTwi with the TWEN/TWWC/TWSTO/TWSTA/TWEA/TWINT bit handles.
The Atmel AVR315 TWI status-code enum (TWI_START..TWI_NO_STATE) — the shared vocabulary between the AVR TWI driver and the generic I2C module.
AVR USART: derives baud rate from UBRR (with U2X double-speed), configures data/stop/parity bits from UCSZ/USB/UPM, and manages the UDRE/TXC/RXC interrupt flags.
Declares AvrUsart over McuUsart with the UCSRnA/B/C and UBRRnL/H bit handles (instance suffix derived from the module name).
AVR Universal Serial Interface: one bit-level engine reused for 3-wire SPI, 2-wire TWI and timer-clocked modes, including start/stop-condition detection.
Declares AvrUsi with the USICR/USISR bit handles and the three-mode (SPI/TWI/timer) state flags.
AVR watchdog: models the WDCE-protected 4-cycle window in which WDP/WDE may change, the timeout period, and the reset-on-overflow behaviour.
Declares AvrWdt over McuWdt plus two generation variants (AvrWdt00 with WDIF/WDIE/WDP3, AvrWdt01 with a fixed 2.097152 s period).
Minimal 8-bit CPU base: constructor nulls the status/stack pointers and reset clears PC and the return address.
The shared 8-bit CPU contract every core honours: m_PC, m_STATUS, m_RET_ADDR, the stack-pointer handles and the INTERRUPT/CALL_ADDR/RET_ADDR hooks.
8051 core: a state machine (RESET/FETCH/OPERAND/EXEC/WRITE) driving ALE/PSEN bus cycles at 1/12 of the read cycle, plus the full 256-opcode decode table.
Declares I51Core with the 8051 SFR addresses, the cpuState_t machine-cycle enum, the addressing-mode bitmask enum and the per-instruction ALU method set.
8051 pin: the port latch gates the output (a port pin cannot drive high when the port register bit is low) and the external-interrupt edge mode is decoded.
Declares I51Pin over McuPin overriding setOutState/scheduleState/ConfExtInt.
8051 port: a port read returns the latched pin state (not the pin direction register), and reset deliberately does not clear the pin state.
Declares I51Port over McuPort overriding reset and readPort and creating I51Pin instances.
8051 timers: the TMOD mode selects 13-bit/16-bit/8-bit/8+8 counter widths, the C/T bit selects external clock, and the GATE bit enables a gate pin (P3.2/P3.3) that stops the timer.
Declares I51Timer over McuTimer with the TMOD bit handles and the gate-pin member.
8051 USART: implements the four SCON modes (synchronous 8-bit, timer-1 asynchronous 8/9-bit, MCU-clock 9-bit) and the SMOD doubling, with a 16-step divide for the timer-1 baud generator.
Declares I51Usart over McuUsart with the SCON/PCON bit handles and the stop-bit-error flag.
6502 core: a cycle-accurate cRESET/cFETCH/cDECODE/cREAD/cEXEC/cWRITE state machine driving phi0/phi1/phi2 and the SYNC/RW bus lines, with 10 ns/20 ns/25 ns bus timing constants.
Declares Mcs65Cpu with the 6502 addressing modes, the status-bit enum, the bus/control pin handles and the member-function-pointer opcode dispatch (m_EXEC).
Decodes an opcode byte into a human-readable mnemonic for the MCU monitor, covering the irregular 6502 opcodes.
Declares Mcs65Interface (Cpu8bits + eElement) whose only job is to publish a "Instruction" string variable to the monitor.
Shared 8-bit MCU CPU base: caches the RAM pointer, program-memory pointer, register window bounds and the STATUS register address; CALL_ADDR pushes the PC and sets the return-cycle count.
Generic 8-bit MCU memory/stack helpers: GET_RAM/SET_RAM route SFR addresses through the watcher mechanism, and PUSH_STACK/POP_STACK implement pre- or post-increment stacks of 1-3 bytes.
PIC12 core: decodes the 12-bit instruction set (OPTION/SLEEP/CLRWDT/TRIS plus the standard ALU/bit/control-transfer opcodes).
Declares Pic12Core over PicMrCore with the TRISGPIO register address.
PIC14 (mid-range) core: binds the FSR/OPTION registers and watches the R0/R1 bank bits to switch the RAM bank.
Declares Pic14Core over PicMrCore, overriding GET_RAM/SET_RAM to resolve the INDF indirect register and the PCL/PCLATH program-counter write.
PIC14 enhanced (mid-range plus) core: 16-deep hardware stack, two FSRs, and the enhanced opcode set (MOVIW/MOVWI/ADDFSR/LSRF/ASRF/SUBWFB/ADDWFC/BRA...).
Declares Pic14eCore over PicMrCore with the FSR0/FSR1/BSR/PCLATH registers and their shadow (SHAD) copies used for interrupt context save/restore.
PIC14e interrupt: saves the CPU context on entry and restores it on exit, around the generic Interrupt::execute/exitInt.
Declares Pic14eInterrupt over PicInterrupt overriding execute and exitInt.

PIC ADC: converts the selected channel voltage over a scheduled conversion time, implements the PCFG analog/digital pin masks per ADC type, and reads the internal temperature sensor / DAC output / FVR buffer for the special channels.
Declares PicAdc plus per-family variants (00/01/02/10/11/20/3) each binding its own ADCON/ADCS/PCFG/ANSEL bit set and Vref rules.
PIC CCP unit: multiplexes capture, compare and PWM modes over one CCPxCON register and one interrupt, dispatching to the capture unit, the compare unit or the PWM unit.
Declares PicCcpUnit over McuModule with the ccpMode_t enum and the three sub-unit handles.
PIC comparators: each chip type wires a different set of pins as +/-, output and reference, and the mode bits choose between them.
Declares PicComp and its per-family subclasses with the CMCON/CMxCON0 bit handles.
PIC configuration word: decodes the config bits into clock source (FOSC), watchdog enable, MCLR enable and (type 04) PLL multiplier, applying them to the internal oscillator and the MCU component.
Declares PicConfigWord over ConfigWord plus five per-family subclasses, and the configClk/configWdt/configRst helpers.
PIC DAC: computes the output voltage from the selected reference (VDD, VREF+ pin or FVR buffer) and the 5-bit DACR value, and drives the output pin voltage.
Declares PicDac over McuDac with the DACCON0/DACCON1 bit handles and the FVR reference.
PIC EEPROM: enforces the 0x55/0xAA unlock sequence within two cycles, schedules a 5 ms write, and clears the WR/RD bits appropriately.
Declares PicEeprom over McuEeprom with the EECON1/EECON2 bit handles and the unlock-sequence state.
PIC input capture: CCPxM selects falling edge, rising edge, or rising edge with a /4 or /16 prescaler.
Declares PicIcUnit over McuIcUnit with a configure(CCPxM) entry point.
PIC interrupt: disables auto-clear and sets the wake-up mask to 0xFF so any interrupt wakes the MCU from sleep.
Declares PicInterrupt over Interrupt; the GIE handling is commented out.
PIC internal oscillator: maps OSCCON (SCS/IRCF/OSCF/SPLLEN) to a frequency, with the PLL multiplier applied for the 8 MHz/32 MHz case, and the config word able to override the choice.
Declares PicIntOsc over McuIntOsc plus three per-family variants with their OSCCON bit sets.
PIC mid-range ALU: implements the instruction set as named methods (MOVWF/CLR/ADDWF/BCF/BSF/CALL/GOTO...) over a shared decode switch, with the Z/C/DC status flag rules.
Declares PicMrCore over Mcu8bits with the 8-deep hardware circular stack, the bank register, the PCL/PCLATH program-counter write and the full ALU method set.
PIC MSSP: the SSPx mode bits select SPI master/slave (with or without SS) or I2C master/slave, and the module disables the other unit before enabling the new one.
Declares PicMssp over McuModule with the SSPMx/SSPEN bit handles and the SPI/TWI unit handles.
PIC output compare and PWM units: the compare actions (toggle/set/clear/special-event) and the PWM duty resolution (CCPRxL plus 2 bits from CCPxCON) drive the OC pin.
Declares PicOcUnit and PicPwmUnit (plus two per-family PWM variants) over McuOcUnit.
PIC pin: switching a pin to analog disables its digital input buffer and forces the port input register bit to 0.
Declares PicPin over McuPin overriding ConfExtInt and setAnalog.
PIC port: reading the port register returns the live pin state (or the RAM value when read from the monitor), and the port-change interrupt flag is cleared on both a read and an output change.
Declares PicPort over McuPort overriding configureA/outChanged/readPort and creating PicPin instances.
PIC sleep module: enabled with sleep mode 1 (idle) and nothing else implemented.
Declares PicSleep over McuSleep with no extra members.
PIC SPI: the SSPEN/CKP/CKE bits set the clock polarity, phase and sample edge; the SSPBUF write starts a master transaction and the end of it clears the BF status bit and raises the interrupt.
Declares PicSpi over McuSpi with the SSPEN/CKP/CKE bit handles.
PIC timers: T0 (prescaler shared with the watchdog, T0CS/T0SE select the external clock), T2 (PR2 period, TOUTPS) and the 16-bit T1/T2 variants.
Declares PicTimer and variants PicTimer0/2/160/161 over McuTimer with the TCON/OPTION/PCON bit handles.
PIC SSP I2C: the SSPCON2 SEN/RSEN/PEN bits generate start/stop, RCEN triggers a master read, and the SSPSTAT BF/RW bits track the buffer state.
Declares PicTwi over McuTwi with the SSPCON/SSPCON2/SSPSTAT bit handles.
PIC USART: TXSTA/RCSTA/SPBRG configure the transmitter and receiver, the baud period is mult*(SPBRG+1) instruction cycles, and the FERR/OERR flags are set from the received frame.
Declares PicUsart over McuUsart with the TXSTA/RCSTA/PIR1/SPBRG bit handles.

PIC voltage reference: the VRR/VR bits select a Vdd-relative ladder, the output pin gets a resistive divider equivalent, and the FVR variant provides fixed 1.024/2.048/4.096 V references plus a temperature sensor.
Declares PicVref and PicVrefE over McuVref with the VRCON/FVRCON bit handles.
PIC watchdog: an 18 ms base period scaled by the prescaler, resets the CPU on overflow, and shares the prescaler with TIMER0 when PSA is set.
Declares PicWdt over McuWdt plus the two variants PicWdt00 (OPTION-driven) and PicWdt01 (WDTCON-driven with SWDTEN).
32-bit register-bit helpers for the QEMU cores; the DataSpace-based getRegBits/writeBitsToReg are commented out, leaving only the inline mask helpers.
Inline 32-bit equivalents of the 8-bit register-bit helpers (getRegBits/setRegBits/clearRegBits/writeRegBits) over regBits32_t.
ESP32 QEMU device: wires the GPIO/IOMUX/I2C/SPI/UART/LEDC modules to their MMIO address windows and builds the 256-entry in/out signal matrix; the matrix body is ~400 lines of literal assignments.
Declares Esp32 over QemuDevice with the APB/CPU frequencies and the GPIO/IOMUX/LED module handles.
ESP32 GPIO: decodes GPIO_OUT/GPIO_ENABLE/GPIO_PINxx/GPIO_FUNCx_IN_SEL_CFG registers into pin state, direction and the peripheral-function routing; also computes the boot strap mode bit permutation.
Declares Esp32Gpio over QemuModule with the 40-pad array and the 256-entry in/out matrix tables.
ESP32 IOMUX: maps each IOMUX register offset to a GPIO pad number and forwards the written value to the GPIO module.
Declares Esp32IoMux over QemuModule with a 40-entry register array and a getMuxGpio offset-to-pad lookup.
ESP32 LEDC peripheral: 8 low-speed timers drive 16 PWM channels; the duty register value is scaled against a fixed 18-bit period and the pin is driven high then low.
Declares Esp32Led plus the LedTimer and LedPwm helper elements.
ESP32 pad: models the 45 kOhm weak pull-up/pull-down, selects one of six IOMUX functions and relabels the pin in the canvas with the current function name.
Declares Esp32Pin over IoPin plus the funcPin struct that links a matrix entry to a peripheral pin pointer and a label.
ESP32 SPI: the SPI_CLOCK/SPI_SLAVE/data-buffer registers set the clock period, master/slave role and start a transfer.
Declares Esp32Spi over QemuSpi.
ESP32 I2C: the I2C_CTR bits choose open-drain vs push-pull and master vs slave, the I2C_CMD opcode field dispatches start/write/read/stop, and setTwiState maps the TWI status codes onto ACK/NACK.
Declares Esp32Twi over QemuTwi with the slave code and last-command state.
ESP32 UART: a 128-byte TX FIFO feeds the shared UsartModule transmitter, UART_CLKDIV sets the baud rate, and UART_CONF0 sets parity/data/stop bits and resets the FIFOs.
Declares Esp32Usart over QemuUsart with the TX/RX FIFO queues.
32-bit variants of regInfo_t and regBits_t for the QEMU (32-bit register space) cores.

QEMU bridge: creates a shared-memory arena (POSIX shm or a Windows file mapping), launches qemu-system-* as a child process, and exchanges register reads/writes and interrupts through the arena; also builds the component context menu.
Declares the qemuArena_t shared-memory struct (simulation time, QEMU time, register data/address, IRQ number/level, action codes) and the QemuDevice component.
QEMU module base: dispatches a read/write action to the subclass register handler and defaults to a plain 32-bit memory slot.
Declares QemuModule, the per-peripheral base that owns an MMIO address window, a clock pointer and a pointer into the shared arena.
Placeholder QEMU output-compare unit: constructor only, no behaviour yet.
Declares QemuOcUnit over QemuModule with no members.
Placeholder QEMU SPI module: the constructor only; the doAction/setMode/endTransaction overrides are commented out.
Declares QemuSpi over QemuModule and SpiModule, exposing the MOSI/MISO/SCK/SS pin pointers so the device can wire them.
Placeholder QEMU timer: constructor only, no counter behaviour.
Declares QemuTimer over QemuModule with bidirectional/direction/one-shot fields that are not yet used.
QEMU I2C module: setMode only forwards to the generic TwiModule when both SCL and SDA pins exist.
Declares QemuTwi over QemuModule and TwiModule with pin-pointer accessors.
QEMU USART: a thin wrapper that enables the shared transmitter/receiver and exposes the TX/RX pin pointers; the arena-based byte transfer is commented out.
Declares QemuUsart over QemuModule and UsartModule with the QEMU_USART_RECEIVE/SENT action codes.
STM32 QEMU device: picks the package and the peripheral counts from the part-number suffix (4/6/8/B/C/D/E), creates the GPIO ports and timers, and implements the AFIO timer-remap wiring.
Declares Stm32 over QemuDevice with the APB1/APB2 frequencies and the port vector.
STM32 AFIO: decodes the MAPR remap bits and calls Stm32::timerRemap to move the timer output-compare pins, and tracks the EXTI source-port selection.
Declares Stm32Afio over QemuModule with the MAPR and EXTICR state.
STM32 timer output-compare channel: the CCMR output-mode bits select frozen/high/low/toggle/forced output and the input prescaler.
Declares Stm32OcUnit over eElement with the CCR/CCMR/OCM state and the target pin.
STM32 pin: honours the alternate-function flag (the port register only drives a pad that is not in alternate mode), models the pull resistor, and paints a pull-dot on the canvas.
Declares Stm32Pin over IoPin with the pull/analog/alternate flags.
STM32 GPIO port: decodes the CRL/CRH configuration nibbles into input/output/open-drain/pull/analog/alternate per pin, and drives the output data register.
Declares Stm32Port over QemuModule with the pin vector.
STM32 SPI: CR1 sets CPHA/CPOL/MSTR/BR/LSBFIRST/SPE, DR starts a transfer, and the status register tracks TXE/RXNE/BUSY.
Declares Stm32Spi over QemuSpi with the CR1/CR2/status registers.

STM32 timer: a special write at offset 0 selects the output-compare channel and drives its pin; the CR1/CR2/SMCR/DIER/SR/EGR/CCMR/CCER/PSC/ARR/CCR register handling is present but mostly commented out.
Declares Stm32Timer over QemuTimer with the four output-compare channels and the register shadow fields.
STM32 I2C: the CR1/CR2/DR/SR1 register handling with the write-0-to-clear error bits, the start/stop condition generation, and the event/error interrupt level computation.
Declares Stm32Twi over QemuTwi with the CR1/CR2/OAR/DR/SR1/SR2/CCR/TRISE registers and the event/error interrupt state.
STM32 USART: CR1/CR2/CR3/SR/DR/BRR handling, the overrun flag cleared by an SR read followed by a DR read, and the interrupt level recomputed from the enabled TXE/TC/RXNE flags.
Declares Stm32Usart over QemuUsart with the DR/SR/divider and interrupt state.
DisplayArea widget: a pixel framebuffer painted at a scale, with Bresenham line drawing, background fill, BGR colour swapping and deferred resizing.
Declares DisplayArea as a QWidget + Updatable + eElement so a script can paint onto a canvas.

ScriptCpu: a whole MCU implemented in AngelScript — registers the ScriptCpu object type, exposes ~40 script-callable methods, and maps script functions (initialize/reset/runStep/voltChanged/INTERRUPT/command) onto the CPU lifecycle.
Declares ScriptCpu over ScriptBase and Mcu8bits, with one asIScriptFunction* handle per script hook and per-property getter/setter maps.
ScriptDisplay: exposes the framebuffer to the script (setPixel/drawLine/setData/setPalette) and decodes a script array-of-arrays into pixels through the palette.
Declares ScriptDisplay over DisplayArea and ScriptPerif with the palette vector and the clear callback.
ScriptPerif constructor/destructor only.
Declares ScriptPerif, the mix-in that lets any MCU peripheral register itself with the script engine and publish its method list.
ScriptPort: mostly stubbed out — the configureA/B/C and reset bodies are commented out; only setExtIntTrig and setScript do anything.
Declares ScriptPort over ScriptBase and McuPort.
ScriptSpi: registers a "SPI <name>" global object with setMode/sendByte and calls the script's byteReceived function at the end of a transaction.
Declares ScriptSpi over McuSpi and ScriptPerif.
ScriptTcp: registers a "TCP <name>" global object with connectToHost/sendMsgToHost/closeSocket and forwards connected/closed/received events into script functions.
Declares ScriptTcp over TcpModule and ScriptPerif with the three script callback handles.
ScriptTwi: registers a "TWI <name>" global object with the master start/write/read/stop calls and lets the script supply the byte to transmit as a return value.
Declares ScriptTwi over McuTwi and ScriptPerif with the byteReceived/writeByte/setTwiState callback handles.
ScriptUsart: registers a "Uart <name>" global object with setBaudRate/setDataBits/sendByte and calls the script on byte received and frame sent.
Declares ScriptUsart over McuUsart and ScriptPerif.

ZX Spectrum ULA: a cycle-accurate model of the video ULA (contention, RAS/CAS/DRAMWE, attribute latches, 448x312 framebuffer, RGB colour tables) built from the equations in Chris Smith's "The ZX Spectrum ULA" book.
Declares ULA_ZX48k with the 448x312 screen buffer, the ULA type enum (5C102E..6C011E) and every bus/control pin handle.

Z80 core: a full machine-cycle/T-state state machine that drives the real Z80 bus (MREQ/IORQ/RD/WR/RFSH/M1/WAIT/BUSACK) and models interrupt modes, HALT, DMA bus requests and every opcode including the CB and ED prefixes.
Declares Z80Core with the register/member-word list published to the monitor and the bus-operation enum.
Lookup tables: the number of machine cycles and the T-states of machine cycle 1 for each of the 256 opcodes in the no-prefix, CB and ED sets.
Z80 register helpers: Z80RegPair (two 8-bit registers as one 16-bit register), Z80Reg16 and Z80Flags (with a changed-bit tracker and the undocumented X/Y flag copies).
Resolves a comma-separated list of bit names into a mask and a base+mask register-bit handle by rotating the mask to find the first bit; writeBitsToReg writes through the watcher mechanism.
Inline register-bit helpers (overrideBits/replaceBits/getRegBits/setRegBits/clearRegBits/writeRegBits) plus the two lookup functions that resolve bit names against the DataSpace tables.
IO-unit base: looks a pin up by name across the registered IoPorts; the port hash is per-instance so several MCUs can coexist.
Declares eIou over eElement, holding the owning Mcu, the CPU pointer, the external clock pin and the IoPort hash.

eMcu: the MCU's electrical/clocking core — reset sequence, external clock edge handling, the run event that advances the clock, the sleep state machine, and the frequency/picoseconds-per-instruction bookkeeping.
Declares eMcu over DataSpace and eIou: the program/ROM/EEPROM memories, the module list, the interrupt controller, the debugger hook and the clocking state.

Mcu component: finds the device's .mcu descriptor file (in the circuit folder, the data folder or the component list), loads the firmware, wires the reset pin and the serial monitor, and forwards mouse events to a script CPU.
Declares the Mcu component: the friend-of-McuCreator entry point, the UI frequency, the EEPROM/program load-save properties and the script-CPU hook.
Generic ADC: samples the selected pin voltage against the reference, schedules the conversion completion and writes the result into the ADCL/ADCH registers.
Declares McuAdc over McuPrescaled with the ADC pins, reference pins, conversion time and resolution members.
Generic comparator: enabled by default, the reference comes from the Vref module, and a change of the comparator output triggers a re-evaluation.
Declares McuComp over McuModule with the +/-, reference and output pins.
ConfigWord: a per-address table of configuration words, with a load-time debug print of the value written.
Declares ConfigWord with a QHash of address to 16-bit configuration word.

The device builder: parses the XML .mcu descriptor into memory blocks, the register map (name/address/reset value/write mask/bit names/aliases) and the peripheral list, then instantiates each peripheral class for the selected core.
Declares McuCreator: one createXxx() per peripheral kind plus the static state the builder carries while parsing one device.
Generic DAC base: the reference voltages, the output value and the enable flags are initialised here; subclasses compute the actual output.
Declares McuDac over McuModule with the reference/output pins and the output-value register pointer.

The register file: readReg/writeReg route every access through the McuSignal callbacks, apply the write mask, and let a callback override the value through m_regOverride (how timers publish their counter and the comparator clears ACO).
Declares DataSpace: the flat RAM vector, the address map, the register write masks, the named register/bit tables and the read/write signal tables.
Generic EEPROM: the address latch and data register, and immediate read/write of the ROM-backed EEPROM.
Declares McuEeprom over McuModule with the address and data register pointers.
Generic input-capture unit: on the selected edge it counts to the prescaler, samples the parent timer's count into the capture registers and raises the interrupt.
Declares McuIcUnit over McuModule with the capture pins/registers, edge polarity and prescaler.

Interrupt controller: a priority-ordered pending list, a running list for nested interrupts, the global enable flag, write-1-to-clear flag semantics, and the "remember a raised flag while disabled" behaviour.
Declares Interrupt and Interrupts: the per-source flag mask/register, the enable/priority/auto-clear/continuous attributes, and the pending/running lists.
Internal/external clock source: the config word decides whether OSC1/OSC2 are I/O, and a clock-out pin toggles at half the instruction period.
Declares McuIntOsc over McuModule with the clock-in/out pin handles, the PLL multiplier and the external-clock flag.
McuModule base: the sleep-mode bitmask bookkeeping (a module only sleeps in the modes its bit is set for) and the interrupt handle.
Declares McuModule: the hooks every peripheral shares — setup/reset, configureA/B/C (register-write callbacks), callBack and callBackDoub, sleep and the three config-bit sets.
Generic output-compare-modifier: when both compare units are active the OCM takes control of the pin, and its state is recomputed on any OC state change.
Declares McuOcm over McuPrescaled with the two OC units and the abstract OutputOcm.
Generic output-compare unit: schedules the compare-match event in picoseconds from the timer tick and the current count (including the PWM duty rotation), and drives the pin on match or overflow.
Declares McuOcUnit over McuModule with the compare-match value, the pin and the ocAct_t action enum.

McuPin: resolves the external-interrupt trigger (including a low-level trigger that fires once at simulation start), reports pin changes to the port, and separates port-drive from peripheral-drive ownership.
Declares McuPin over IoPin with the extIntTrig_t enum, the out/dir control flags and the pin mask.

McuPort: aggregates pin changes into the port input register (written straight to RAM), raises the port-change interrupt, and applies output/direction register changes only to the bits that actually changed.
Declares McuPort over McuModule with the out/in/dir register pointers, the pin vector and the direct-control API.
Prescaler: selects a value from the prescaler list by index, clamping an out-of-range index to 0.
Declares McuPrescaled over McuModule with the prescaler-selection bits, the index and the list of prescaler values.

McuSignal: a typed, masked, LIFO callback list used for every register read/write hook. New callbacks are PREPENDED so that an interrupt flag clear runs after the register-write callback (interrupts are created first).
Generic sleep module: the wake-up callback puts the MCU back into running mode.
Declares McuSleep over McuModule with the sleep mode byte and the enable flag.
Generic SPI module for MCUs: initialises the shared SpiModule and clears the status register.
Declares McuSpi over McuPrescaled and SpiModule with the data and status register pointers.

Generic timer: the counter value is DERIVED from the simulator clock (calcCounter) rather than incremented, overflow is scheduled as an absolute sim time and only re-scheduled when it actually changes, and the tick period is the prescaler times the instruction period.
Declares McuTimer over McuPrescaled with the count, overflow-match, tick period, time offset and the output-compare/input-capture unit lists.
Generic TWI module: a bit-level I2C master/slave state machine driving the SDA/SCL pins with a half-clock-period event, implementing start/stop/ack/read/write.
Declares McuTwi over McuPrescaled and TwiModule with the address/data/status register pointers.
Two POD structs shared by every core: regInfo_t (register address + reset value) and regBits_t (a bit field of a register: base bit, mask, live pointer and address).
Generic MCU USART: raises the data-register-empty interrupt, prints the sent frame to the serial monitor and overrides the receive register with the received byte.
Declares McuUsart over McuModule and UsartModule with the 9th-bit (TXB8/RXB8) bit handles.
Generic voltage-reference module: holds the reference value and notifies the registered callback modules when it changes.
Declares McuVref over McuModule with the output pin and the callback list.
Generic watchdog base: only initialises the state; the real behaviour lives in the AVR and PIC subclasses.
Declares McuWdt over McuPrescaled with the fuse, overflow-interrupt, overflow-reset and period fields.

One-Wire (DS18B20-style) slave: decodes the pulse width on the single wire to recover bits, implements the reset / search-ROM / match-ROM / skip-ROM / read-ROM commands and generates a CRC8-checked ROM.
Declares OneWire with the 1-Wire state and command enums, the ROM array and the pulse-timing members.

AngelScript host: creates the engine and context, enables the JIT, resolves #include directives (relative to the script folder or to the bundled scriptlib), compiles the sections and reports script errors with file/line.
Declares ScriptBase over eElement: the AngelScript engine, module and context handles plus the compile/execute helpers.
ScriptModule: a generic MCU peripheral whose configureA/B/C, callBack and callBackDoub hooks are implemented in AngelScript, looked up by exact function declaration after compilation.
Declares ScriptModule over ScriptBase and McuModule with one asIScriptFunction* handle per hook.

Shared SPI engine: a bit-level master that toggles the clock on a scheduled half-period and a slave that samples on the configured edges, with the lead/sample/tail edge triple defining the four SPI modes.
Declares SpiModule over eClockedDevice and TransModule with the MOSI/MISO/SCK/SS pins and the edge configuration.
TCP bridge for scripted MCUs: opens QTcpSocket connections to a host/port, and delivers received text, connected and disconnected events back to the script.
Declares TcpModule over eElement, Updatable and TransModule with the per-link connection record and the virtual event hooks.
TransModule: the serial-monitor plumbing shared by every peripheral that can send or receive bytes (TWI, SPI, USART, OneWire, TCP).
Declares TransModule with the module name, the monitor window handle and the printOut/printIn helpers.
Shared I2C engine: the master state machine issues start/stop and reads/writes bits on the SDA line with SCL, and the slave side detects its address and acknowledges.
Declares TwiModule over eClockedDevice and TransModule with the I2C state enum, the TWI mode enum and the SDA/SCL pins.
Shared USART engine: the baud-rate period, the data-bit count/parity/stop-bit configuration, the synchronous-mode clock generator, and the UartTR base with its per-module pin multiplexing.
Declares UsartModule over TransModule plus the UartSync clock generator and the UartTR base class.
UART receiver: detects the start bit, samples the frame on the baud period, checks the stop and parity bits, and maintains a 2-entry FIFO with overrun and frame-error flags.
Declares UartRx over UartTR with the FIFO, the ignore-data (multiprocessor) flag and the start-bit state.
UART transmitter: builds the frame (start, data, optional parity, stop bits) and shifts it out one bit per baud period.
Declares UartTx over UartTR with processData/startTransmission.
Template helpers that attach a member-function callback to a register address, a list of register names or a list of bit names, creating the McuSignal on demand.
